objective: Check that spread_decomposition splits the population variance of per-track descriptors exactly into within-cluster and between-cluster parts, and that the per-block between-cluster share behaves correctly in the limiting cases.
module: CFMU (cluster feature unit), part of FYP-1. Not active in Deliverable III; the maths is implemented and tested ahead of the clustering step (§10.3), which is not built yet.
assumptions: Synthetic inputs: x is a 20 x 4 matrix of standard-normal values and labels are random cluster ids in {0, 1, 2}, both from numpy default_rng(0). Some steps replace the labels or data with degenerate cases.

steps.execution: Call spread_decomposition(x, labels) on the random 20 x 4 data with 3 clusters.
steps.result: total_sd squared equals the population variance x.var(axis=0) per feature (rtol 1e-10), and within_sd squared plus between_sd squared equals total_sd squared. Observed: as expected.

steps.execution: Call spread_decomposition with all 20 labels set to 0 and one block 'all' covering columns [0, 1, 2, 3].
steps.result: between_sd is 0 for every feature and between_share['all'] is exactly 0.0. Observed: as expected.

steps.execution: Call spread_decomposition with labels 0..19 (every track its own cluster) and block 'a' covering columns [0, 1].
steps.result: within_sd is 0 for every feature (atol 1e-12) and between_share['a'] is 1.0 (assertAlmostEqual). Observed: as expected.

steps.execution: Call spread_decomposition on a 5 x 2 matrix of ones, labels [0, 0, 1, 1, 2], block 'b' covering columns [0, 1].
steps.result: Total variance is zero, so between_share['b'] is returned as 0.0 instead of a division by zero. Observed: as expected.
